name: Turkish citizenship by investment: statistics
description: Long-format observations on Turkish citizenship acquisitions, the investment route, foreign property purchases, threshold and rule changes, and 2026 enforcement action. Every record names its source and an as-of date. value is null where the figure is not published.

conventions.value: Number where published; null where not published. published flags which.
conventions.source: Named for every record. Where a figure reached the public through a ministerial statement or a parliamentary answer rather than a published table, the source field says so.
conventions.asOf: Date the figure was published or restated, not the date this file was built.

notKnown: Goc Idaresi Baskanligi publishes no citizenship-acquisition statistics series. Annual figures reach the public through ministerial statements and parliamentary answers.
Annual citizenship acquisitions for 2018, 2022, 2023 and 2026 are not published. The series is non-monotonic, so it must not be interpolated.
There is no annual investment-route series, and no published application, approval, rejection or backlog count.
No Turkish authority publishes an end-to-end processing time for the investor route.
TUIK 2025 nationality counts for China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Afghanistan and Kuwait are not published.
No 2026 year-to-date nationality or province breakdown of foreign house sales is published.
No official average transaction value for foreign property purchases is published by TUIK, TKGM or TCMB.
The revised TUIK series year mapping for 2013 to 2021 is derived by ratio matching, not read off an official table.
Appraisal report validity: the Kilavuz of 1 February 2024 states 3 months, post-2026 secondary reporting states 12 months. The sources disagree and the 9 December 2024 Kilavuz could not be read.
The current status of the closed-neighbourhood regime for residence permits is unresolved. No official announcement lifting or restating the 2022 position was located.
The legal instrument behind the USD 200,000 residence-permit property threshold of 16 October 2023 could not be identified.
Overlap between the cumulative 6,134 cancellations and the 687 and 1,070 criminal-file identifications is unquantified.

figuresInCirculationNotUsed.reason: Inconsistent with five published TUIK cumulatives, which give 1,306.
Implausible against 110 units in April 2026 alone; not used.

figuresInCirculationNotUsed.claim: About 15,000 investment-route principals and 40,000 people to end-2025
figuresInCirculationNotUsed.reason: Undated source with no primary link; contradicts the Interior Minister figures by a factor of about 3.5. Not used.
A derived sum of 687 and 1,070 published by a trade outlet, not by any authority, with overlap unclarified. Carried in the data only as a flagged derived record.

figuresInCirculationNotUsed.claim: Automatic 25 per cent uplift on valuations
figuresInCirculationNotUsed.reason: No primary text; described as unreliable by practitioners.

figuresInCirculationNotUsed.claim: Real-estate threshold rising to USD 600,000 or USD 500,000
figuresInCirculationNotUsed.reason: Never enacted. The consolidated Regulation still reads USD 400,000.
